page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by four NVIDIA Volta V100 graphics processing units, delivering a combined total of 64 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. The host system features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, backed by 128 GB of system memory and 33 MB of L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps under the KVM hypervisor. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-threaded host capabilities alongside conservative single-thread compute. The Intel Xeon 8163 processor achieved 23,575.63 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 21,092.78 on the PassMark CPU benchmark, placing it squarely in the middle tier of general compute capacity. In contrast, single-thread performance reflects its generational age, producing lower metrics in stress-ng single-core (1,103.89) and compression workloads such as gzip (19.1 GB/sec) and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (7.53 GB/sec). Large-block memory bandwidth sustains 118.4 GB/sec read and 57.05 GB/sec write throughput.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the resource profile prioritizes parallel accelerator density over cutting-edge CPU performance. The presence of four discrete V100 accelerators delivers substantial matrix computing capability, but the lack of integrated local NVMe storage means I/O-intensive datasets require network block volumes, introducing potential network latency. This server is best suited for deep learning training, multi-GPU batch inference, distributed graphics rendering, molecular dynamics simulations, and parallel scientific computing workflows that process workloads primarily within GPU memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance equipped with four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs providing 64 GB of aggregate VRAM. Powered by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz and 128 GB of RAM, the system operates on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization with 10 Gbps baseline network throughput. Local storage is not provided, requiring reliance on attached network storage. Synthetic benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU and memory throughput, alongside weaker single-core processing capabilities. The high GPU-to-CPU ratio makes this configuration efficient for multi-GPU machine learning training, AI inference, video processing, and GPU-bound scientific simulations.
